test_title: PYST 16: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - Quant (Held On 27 Jun, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 20 days, 30 days and 60 days, respectively, working alone. How soon can the work be done if A is assisted by B and C each on every alternate day?
solution:
**Given:**

A, B, and C can do a piece of work in 20 days, 30 days, and 60 days respectively

**Concept used:**

Efficiency = Total Work/Time required

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 60 units (LCM of 20, 30 and 60)

⇒ Efficiency of A = 60/20 = 3 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 60/30 = 2 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = 60/60 = 1 unit/day

According to the question, A is assisted by B and C on alternate days

Work done by (A + B) = 5 units

Work done by (A + C) = 4 units

⇒ In one cycle (2 days), 9 units of work is completed

⇒ In six cycles (12 days), 54 units of work will be completed

Remaining work = 6 units

Work done on 13th day (A + B) = 5 units

Remaining work = 1 unit

Now, (A + C) will be working

⇒ Time required by (A + C) for 1 unit = 1/4 days

⇒ Total time required = 13 + (1/4) = 53/4 days
